sentences.text:
Binnya Mathew vs Benjaram Raju on 11 December, 2024
 Honourable Smt.Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.89 Of 2019
Judgment:

Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - IX Additional District Judge at Kamareddy, in M.V.O.P. No.42 of 2013 dated 12.05.2017, the present appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - IX Additional District Judge at Kamareddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case according to the appellant/claimant are as under:
a) On 13.06.2012, while the petitioner was proceeding on his TVS Apache Motorcycle bearing No. AP 25 AC 9739 along with one Yousuf Khan (pillion rider) from Kamareddy towards Nizamabad, Indica Car bearing No. AP 23-G-0263 being driven by its driver from wrong side in a rash and negligent manner at a high speed and dashed against the TVS Motorcycle of petitioner in opposite direction at about 11:30 P.M at Adloor Yellaredy Village road bridge, due to which, the petitioner and pillion rider fell down from the motorcycle and the alleged crime MGP,J vehicle ran over them, as a result of which, they both sustained multiple fractures.
b) The petitioner took treatment as inpatient in Government Area Hospital,
Kamareddy and also in a private hospital at Kamareddy.

The Police, Sadashivnagar,
Nizamabad District registered a case in First Information Report (FIR) No. 113/2012 under Section 338 of Indian Penal Code, 1806 against the driver of unknown vehicle,
which hit the motorcycle of the petitioner and after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the crime vehicle i.e., Indica car bearing No. AP 23 G 0263.

The claimant filed claim petition before the Tribunal under Section 166 (1)(a) of the Motor Vehicle Act claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the accident against the respondent Nos.1 and 2, who are the insured and insurer of the crime vehicle involved in the accident.

c) In reply to the claim of the petitioner, respondent No.1 i.e., owner of the crime vehicle i.e., Indica Car Bearing No. AP.23.G.0263 remained ex-parte and whereas the respondent No. 2/Insurance Company filed counter denied the manner in which the accident occurred, the age, avocation and income of the appellant/claimant.
It is contended that the owner and insurer of the motorcycle were not made party, hence claim MGP,J petition is not maintainable.

Further, the alleged accident is a case of contributory negligence of drivers of both vehicle i.e., motorcycle and the alleged crime car,
as such the insurance company shall not be made liable to pay compensation.

It is also contended Binnya Mathew vs Benjaram Raju on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168788571/
1 that driver of the alleged crime vehicle was not having a valid driving licence at the time of accident and insurance company has not received any report in Form No-54 from concerned police station as per Section 158 (6) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 intimating regarding the vehicular accident, which is in violation of condition stipulated in the insurance policy and to maintain any claim.

sentences.text: It is further contended that the amount claimed is excessive and exorbitant and prayed for dismissal of the case.
d) Based on the rival contentions, the Tribunal has framed the following three issues.
1. Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Indica Car Bearing No. AP 23 G 0263?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for a compensation, if so from whom and what amount?
3. To what relief ?
MGP,J e)
On behalf of the appellant/claimant, he got examined himself as PW1 apart from examining PWs 2 and 3 i.e., orthopedic doctors, who treated the appellant/claimant and got marked Exs. A1 to A11.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, none were examined, however, got marked Ex. B1 Insurance policy copy on their side.

f) The learned Tribunal after evaluation of oral and documentary evidence available on record,
partly allowed the claim of the petitioner by awarding compensation of Rs.5,22,710/-(Five Lakhs Twenty Two Thousand Seven Hundred Ten Only) with costs and interest @ 7.5 % per annum from the date of filing of the petition till the date of realization, to be deposited by respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally within one month.

Challenging the quantum of compensation,
appellant/claimant filed the present Appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

3. Heard both sides and perused the entire material available on record including the grounds of Appeal.
4.
The undisputed facts are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 have not preferred any appeal against the impugned order passed by the learned Tribunal.

There is no dispute with regard MGP,J to the manner of the accident as the Tribunal by relying on Exs.A1 (FIR), A2 (Charge-sheet) and A3 (injury certificate) answered issue No.1 holding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Indica Car bearing No. AP 23- G-0263 and that the claimant sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
There is also no dispute that the insurance policy under Ex.B1 was subsisting as on the date of accident.

5. The prime contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the Tribunal erred in awarding only Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferance without considering that the claimant sustained 80% disability as per Ex.A11.

Binnya Mathew vs Benjaram Raju on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168788571/
2

6. As per Ex.A3 wound certificate issued by Medical Officer in charge, Government Area Hospital,
Kamareddy, the petitioner sustained laceration wound over the right mid arm of about 10 x 2 x 2 centimeter in size traumatic amputation of right arm with distal arm missing and grievous injuries all over the body.
In order to prove the above injuries, the petitioner got examined PW2, who has provided treatment to him.
PW2 has corroborated the evidence of the petitioner/PW1 to the extent that the petitioner sustained the injuries as mentioned in Ex.A3.
Though PW2 was cross examined by the learned counsel MGP,J for the respondent No.2, nothing was elicited to discard the evidence of PWs 1 and 2.

Thus, there is no dispute that the petitioner has sustained injuries as deposed by PWs 1 and 2 coupled with Ex.A3.
7.
Now coming to the disability, the petitioner relied upon the documentary evidence under Ex.A11 to show that he has sustained disability of 80%.

Ex.A11 was issued by Civil Assistant Surgeon,
District Hospital Nizamabad.
In order to establish Ex.A11, the petitioner got examined PW3, who is the Civil Assistant Surgeon, Government Hospital Nizamabad and also the member of the Medical Board in the year 2012.

PW3 deposed that on 02.11.2012 PW1 came before the Medical Board with posttraumatic right upper limb amputation of right hand upto mid humerus level and after examination of the petitioner physically and clinically they assessed 80% disability for upper limb and that they have issued Ex.A11.
8.
In the cross examination PW3 admitted that in EX.A11 it was not valued for legal purpose.
PW3 categorically deposed in his chief examination that they assessed 80% of the disability for upper limb.
Thus, it is clear that the disability assessed by the Medical Board under Ex.A11 is only to the extent of right MGP,J hand but not to entire body.
If 80% refers only to the arm, its contribution to the whole-body rating would be calculated.
The arm is typically considered 60% of the whole person.
If the arm is 100% disabled, the whole-body impairment might be around 60%.
If the arm is 80% impaired, the whole-body impairment could be 48%.
Thus, the disability of the petitioner to the extent of amputation of his right hand upto humerus level can be fixed around 50% so far as impairment of the whole body is concerned.
9. The learned Tribunal without calculating the disability as per the procedure, has awarded Rs.3,25,000/- as compensation towards loss of earnings and disability.
No reason was assigned by the Tribunal as to what was the basis to arrive at Rs.3,25,000/- as compensation towards loss of earnings and disability.
10. The claim of the petitioner is that he was drawing Rs.15,000/- per month by doing tyre re-trading manufacturer and earning more than Rs.15,000/- per month.
But except his self serving testimony, no oral or documentary proof is adduced by the petitioner to substantiate that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
In the absence of any oral or MGP,J documentary evidence, by considering the avocation of the petitioner as tyre re-trading manufacturer, his income can be fixed @ Rs.6,000/- per month.
The age of the petitioner as per Exs.A2, A3 and A11 is 21 years.
As the petitioner is aged below 40 years and amputation of his right hand to humerus level will certainly reduce his ability to work in future.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 1 the Honourable Apex Court observed that if the age of the deceased/injured is less than 40 years, future prospects @ 40% may be taken if Binnya Mathew vs Benjaram Raju on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168788571/
3 the deceased/injured was self employed.

sentences.text: The salary fixed by this Court is Rs.6,000/- and the petitioner is entitled for addition of 50% towards future prospects to the established income.

Thus,
40% of Rs.6,000/- would come to Rs.2,400/-.

When 40% of future prospects is added to Rs.6,000/-, the monthly salary of the petitioner would come to Rs.8,400/- (Rs.6,000/- +
Rs.2400/-).
As per the decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in Smt. Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 2, the appropriate multiplier for a person aged between 21 to 25 years is '18'.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the quantum of compensation under the head 'permanent disability' would 1 2017 ACJ 2700 2 (2009) 6 SCC 121 MGP,J come to Rs.9,07,200/- (Rs.8,400/- x 50% x 12 x 18).
Thus, the claimant is entitled for Rs.9,07,200/- under the head 'loss of income due to disability'.

11. Due to the grievous injuries, certainly the petitioner would have remained bedridden for a period of at least three months and during such period there was not scope for him to earn anything by any means.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.18,000/- (Rs.6,000/- x 3 months) towards loss of earnings.
12. Furthermore, due to the above mentioned injuries, the petitioner may not be able to discharge his day to day activities without the assistance of an attendant during the bed ridden period.

Thus,
the claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges.

13. As can be seen from the impugned order, the Tribunal awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferance, Rs.25,000/- towards extra nourishment, Rs.10,000/- towards transportation charges and Rs.62,710/- towards medical treatment.
So far as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the above heads is concerned, this Court is of the opinion that they are just and reasonable and no interference is warranted.
MGP,J 14.

In view of the foregoing discussion in the above paragraphs, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned order passed by the learned Tribunal is required to be modified only to the extent of awarding compensation under the heads 'permanent disability', 'loss of earnings' and 'attendant charges' as indicated above.

Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the compensation under various heads, as follows:

. No .

Name of the head Compensation  entitled by the  claimant in (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferance 1,00,000/-
 2. Transportation charges 10,000/-
 3. Medical treatment 62,710/-
 4. Permanent disability 9,07,200/-
 5. Attendant Charges 10,000/-

4  6.

Extra Nourishment 25,000/-
 7. Loss of earnings (Rs.6,000 x 3 18,000/-
 months)
 Total 11,32,910/-
15.

In the result, the Appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation from Rs.5,22,710/- to Rs.11,32,910/- which shall carry interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till the date of realization payable by the respondents jointly and severally.
The respondent Nos.1 and 2 MGP,J (owner and insurer) are directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
On such deposit, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to withdraw the same without furnishing any security.
However, the petitioner/appellant shall pay the deficit court fee on the enhanced compensation.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
